text:
anya: Heads-up from support: a customer copied the browser quickstart from the README into a public CodePen and leaked their API key to the internet. The snippet shows `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: window.REDWOOD_API_KEY })` in a browser example and the docs suggest setting a global for quick testing.

miguel: oh no. We definitely shouldn't be encouraging client-side API keys. Which README exactly? link?

anya: docs/quickstarts/browser/README.md. The page has both a server-side and a browser demo, but the prominent 'Try it in browser' code block uses a global apiKey variable and the copy button copies it verbatim. Support had to tell the user to rotate their key.

support-bot: Ticket #22011 linked: user reported their key leaked from a public gist. Support recommended immediate key rotation and created a help doc on rotating keys.

samir: we added that browser example ages ago as a convenience but never added a clear warning. Two immediate fixes: 1) remove direct apiKey usage in the browser snippet, replace with a safe proxy pattern (POST to /api/proxy that injects key server-side), 2) add a bold security callout above the snippet warning never to store secret keys in client-side code.

miguel: agree. Also change the copy button behavior so it won't copy the comments that suggest `window.REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Maybe we should make the browser example a separate collapsible sandbox that explicitly states "server proxy required".

anya: proposed replacement browser snippet:
```html
<!-- NOT FOR PRODUCTION: use a server proxy instead -->
<script>
async function callResponses(input) {
  // POST to your server route which calls Redwood with the API key
  const r = await fetch('/api/proxy/responses', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ input })
  });
  return r.json();
}
</script>
```
And add an accompanying server example in Node/Express that reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from env and forwards the request.

samir: plus a short paragraph explaining why client-side keys are bad and a one-liner showing how to mint short-lived session tokens for public demos (our tokens service example). We have an internal example for ephemeral tokens, can we surface that?

miguel: yes, surface the ephemeral token example but make it clearly labeled as advanced. For the quickstart keep the simple proxy pattern and a link to the ephemeral token guide for demo apps.

docs-bot: Reminder: tag PR with docs/quickstart and security. Include an explicit "DO NOT put API keys in client-side code" banner and add a short troubleshooting blurb for leaked keys (rotate immediately, restrict key scopes). Also add a small checklist item to the docs PR template: verify no examples promote client-side secret usage.

anya: I opened PR #7209: replaces browser example with proxy-first snippet, adds server-side Node/Express forwarder sample, includes security callout, and links to ephemeral token guide. cc @miguel @samir for review.

samir: left a minor wording suggestion and asked to include an example of how to call the proxy from React (fetch + setState) so folks copying from the quickstart get a ready-to-run snippet for SPA.

miguel: LGTM after that tiny addition. Also filed follow-up #7210 to scan docs for `window.REDWOOD_API_KEY` and similar patterns (grep + PRs).

anya: thanks 60a I'll also add a small test to our docs CI that looks for patterns like `window.` followed by `REDWOOD` to catch accidental client-side key mentions.

support-bot: closing ticket #22011 as docs fix in progress; user rotated key and confirmed deletion from public gist.

docs-bot: Suggestion: update the docs style guide to include a section "secure quickstarts" with common pitfalls (client-side keys, baking .env into images, copy button behavior). That would centralize these lessons.

miguel: great idea. Can someone add that to the docs backlog? I'll create the epic.

anya: done. Added to docs backlog epic and note in the PR description. Merging after CI.
